title: "[feature] st.tabs state persistence and CSS key class #14332" Breaks tab lazy loading
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

[[feature] st.tabs state persistence and CSS key class](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/14332) introduced a bug in tracking the open state of tabs. In my program, I have a multi-tab configuration interface with the last tab being the validation tab. At the bottom of each tab is a navigation button to go forward or back to the next/prev tab. The validation tab has a submit/update button that publishes to the API.

Symptoms show when we do the following in order:
- open an object in the configurator
- change any property or setting in one of the non-validation tabs
- navigate to the validation tab using the nav buttons, not by clicking on the tab
- Click "Update"

Instead of updating the object and taking us to the experiment list, we get dropped back to the tab that had the change, like Settings. The update fails.

Here's how the tabs are instantiated:

```
    tabs_key = f"{prefix}_tabs"

    def _switch_tab(tab: str) -> None:
        st.session_state[tabs_key] = tab

    tab_groups, tab_steps, tab_pattern, tab_settings, tab_validation = st.tabs(
        ["Groups", "Steps", "Sensor Read Pattern", "Settings", "Validation"],
        on_change="rerun",
        key=tabs_key,
    )
```

Here's an example of the nav buttons:

```
        back_col, _, next_col = st.columns([1, 3, 1])
        with back_col:
            st.button(
                "Read Pattern",
                icon=":material/arrow_back:",
                key=f"{prefix}_settings_back",
                type="secondary",
                width="stretch",
                on_click=_switch_tab,
                args=("Sensor Read Pattern",),
            )
        with next_col:
            st.button(
                "Validation",
                icon=":material/arrow_forward:",
                icon_position="right",
                key=f"{prefix}_settings_next",
                type="primary",
                width="stretch",
                on_click=_switch_tab,
                args=("Validation",),
            )
```

Not using `.open` allows me to workaround at the expense of losing lazy loading.

```
    # if tab_validation.open:
    if True:
        with tab_validation:
```

hey [USER] ! I've dug into this and have a clear picture of what's happening.

The bug is in how `tab.open` is evaluated after a programmatic tab switch via `session_state`. When `_switch_tab()` sets the session state key, the backend knows the intended tab — but on the next rerun, `tab.open` reads from the frontend's `elementStates` (introduced in #14332), which hasn't been updated yet. So `tab_validation.open` evaluates to `False` even though the user navigated there, causing the tab content to be skipped and the Update callback to never execute.

The fix should be in `Tabs.tsx` — specifically in `getPersistedTabIndex()`, where the backend-set widget value should take priority over the locally cached `elementStates` when both exist.
